# XER Schedule Check: DCMA 14-point assessment of a Primavera P6 XER file

> Free, in-browser DCMA 14-point schedule check for Primavera P6 .xer exports. It reads the XER tables, recomputes early and late dates and total float on each activity's own calendar with P6's relationship, lag-calendar, constraint and progress rules (equal to P6's stored values on 19,820 of 19,822 open activities, 99.99%, in six public files from P6 5.0 to 24.12; free float on 19,820; the late dates P6 keeps for finished activities on 1,550 of 1,555), runs the 14 points with the DCMA thresholds and a 600-day critical path test, and lists every activity behind each finding (files from converters and other tools are read too, with a warning for each guess), plus logic loops, out-of-sequence progress, open finishes, and durations edited after the last schedule run (an unstarted activity whose stored dates span a different duration than the file holds; the tool reschedules with the implied durations and says how many stored-date differences the edits explain: 25 of 25 on a public P6 17.12 file, 300 of 300 planted edits found on six others). Lags changed after the last schedule run are named too, longer or shorter, with the lag P6 used: P6 writes two relationship dates on every link at each schedule run (TASKPRED aref and arls, shown on no P6 screen), decoded here on 40,476 of 40,476 links on six public P6 files, so a lag edited since reads straight back (1,200 of 1,200 planted edits recovered exactly, 1,200 of 1,200 links added after the run named, no false listing); a link the stored dates break is also listed with the lag the dates leave room for, and the tool reschedules with the lags P6 used. Microsoft Project schedules saved as XML (MSPDI) are read into the same tables and go through every check (early finish, late finish and total float equal Project's stored values on 2,442 of 2,491 open tasks in 102 files saved by Project 2002 to 2019, with each task on its resources' calendars and in-progress work restarting at its Resume date as Project schedules them; the rest are contoured or timephased work, split tasks and manual tasks). It also compares two monthly updates of one project: progress claimed, actual dates edited after reporting, logic, duration, constraint and calendar changes, float used, driving-path changes, and a half-step run that splits the finish movement into progress and revisions. A windows analysis takes every update of a job at once, sorts them by data date, and for each window between two data dates gives the finish movement, its progress and revision split, and the activities on the driving path behind it; the windows add up to the whole movement. A Monte Carlo risk run draws every open activity's remaining duration from a triangular range (a default the user replaces, per-activity days, or three-point ranges read from the schedule's own activity UDFs such as Optimistic / Most Likely / Pessimistic Duration; a range with a negative or out-of-order point keeps the default range and is named in the warnings) and gives P10/P50/P80/P90 finish dates, the chance of the forecast and must-finish dates, and each activity's criticality index and sensitivity; an optional risk register (events with a probability and a delay range on named activities) shows the contingency the events add at P80 and ranks each event by how far it moves the finish. Resource levelling delays not-started activities until every resource stays within its maximum units per hour from the file (by early start, then the file's levelling priority, then total float; successors carried by the same CPM engine) and gives the levelled finish, every activity moved and the resource that moved it, peak use before and after, a lower bound no levelling can beat, and a crew-size what-if. The assessment, comparison and risk run feed a written review an owner's rep can print to PDF and send: corrections ranked high, medium and low with the exact activities behind each, and, after a risk run, a finish date risk section (the ranges assumed, P10-P90 with and without the register, events ranked, the activities that drive the finish) with corrections for a must-finish date met in under 80% of runs, near-critical activities off the driving path that drive the finish in a quarter or more of runs, and a forecast met in under half the runs with no stated contingency; after a windows analysis over the job's updates, a delay-by-window section with corrections asking the contractor to justify revisions that moved the finish later and to show the recovery plan where revisions took back time progress lost; and, optionally, an appendix listing every activity behind every correction. The longest path takes every driving branch into the finish and is checked against the flag P6 stores (261 of 261 open activities on five public files; on a sixth, P6's flags contradict its own stored float and the page says so). A look-ahead (1-26 weeks, 3 by default, from the data date or a later start) lists the work in the window by WBS with a bar per working day on each activity's calendar and a make-ready check from the logic (ready, waits on named look-ahead work with its date, waits on work outside the window, no predecessor; the driving link or constraint; out-of-sequence work), printable as a landscape sheet and as CSV; on seven public P6 files its windows hold the activities P6's own stored dates put there on 6,476 of 6,479. A constraints log (materials, permits, RFIs, crews: the site team's spreadsheet, pasted or as CSV, columns found by name) merges into the make-ready check: each row gets the date the schedule needs it by, the latest start before a deadline moves, and a status (overdue, late, no date, on track, cleared); logic-ready work with an open row is "constrained"; and the finish is recomputed as if every row clears on its expected date, each late row also alone, ranked by how far it moves the finish (equal to the same dates as P6 start-on-or-after constraints on six public files). A row past P6's late start is labelled by what it does: moves the finish or a deadline; within the slack the calendars leave, moving nothing; or on a path that misses a deadline by less than the path that drives it, so the deadline is no later (65 planted rows on six public files: the 38 read as moving something all do, the 27 read as moving nothing move nothing, and 21 of 21 probed one working hour past their bound do move). Multiple float paths to any activity, an interim milestone as much as the finish: path 1 is the driving chain into it, each later path the next least float relative to it (how far an activity can slip before it moves that one activity), with a CSV of every path. Calendar slack: the float P6's late dates miss where a finish-to-finish or start-to-finish link joins calendars with different working days (a successor that may finish in its own non-work time gives a 7-day predecessor that time too), listed by link and by activity (188 activities gaining 1-17 h on the public hotel file, each checked by rescheduling). Earned value from the cost (or labour hours) on the resource assignments: budget, planned, earned and actual, SPI, CPI, TCPI, three estimates at completion, earned schedule SPI(t), a monthly S-curve with the forecast over the recomputed dates, a WBS breakdown and cost-loading checks (unloaded work, cost on unstarted work, progress with nothing spent, front-loading, overruns, and actuals that equal earned value because P6 computed them from progress: 2,020 of 2,020 activities on a public hospital file). Earned value by window across a series of updates: each period's earned value against what the previous update's own forecast promised by the next data date (1.000 when the period went as that update said, which a re-planned baseline cannot flatter), against the earliest update's planned curve held as baseline, and against what was spent, naming the activities that earned less than promised, spent well past what they earned, changed budget, or had earned value or actuals taken back (on series built from four public files: 435 of 435 planted slips and 250 of 250 planted overruns named, no other activity). A time impact analysis inserts a delay event's fragnet (new activities with working days, predecessors, successors, an event date; or days added to an existing activity) into an update and recomputes it: the finish and every open milestone's movement in working days, the float each activity gives up, each named event alone and the overlap between them (concurrency), a printable exhibit, and the impacted XER to import into P6; days added to a milestone are refused, and activities whose expected finish date absorbs the delay, or whose successors are tied only to their start, are named (eval/tia-check-2026-11-20.md). A Gantt chart draws the WBS tree in P6's order with a summary bar per node and a bar per activity (actual, remaining, critical by the project's setting or by the longest path, milestones, data date), with level of effort and WBS summary activities given the dates P6 gives them (305 of 305 equal P6's stored dates on the public files), and, with a baseline file, each activity's baseline bar and finish variance in working days; printable and as CSV (eval/gantt-check-2026-11-20.md). The chart groups by the file's activity codes too (responsibility, area, phase, trade; nested codes as a tree; a code then the WBS), every activity under the value the file gives it: 1,239,716 of 1,239,716 placements on 92 charts from four public files (eval/activity-codes-2026-11-21.md). An XER converts to Microsoft Project XML (open it in Project, ProjectLibre or GanttProject): WBS as summary tasks, activity IDs in Text1, calendars with every exception, links and lags, constraints, progress, baseline, resources and assignments, activity codes as Text2..Text30 named after each code type (276,042 of 276,042 code values on four public files read back the same, and MPXJ reads every one under the right field, eval/msproject-codes-2026-11-21.md); activity user-defined fields as named Number1..20, Cost1..10, Date1..10 and spare Text fields (codes and text UDFs share the 29 text fields by how many activities each fills; 42,971 of 42,971 UDF values on two public files and a planted one read back the same through this tool and MPXJ, eval/msproject-udfs-2026-11-21.md); level of effort as manual tasks with their links in the notes; on six public P6 files every activity (21,422) and relationship (54,843) reads back unchanged and MPXJ reads the same values from both files on every field but one (eval/msproject-check-2026-11-21.md). The other way, a Microsoft Project XML file converts to a P6 XER for P6's import (a planner in Project asked for an XER): WBS under one project node, activity IDs (a text field named Activity ID, else A + row x 10), calendars, links, constraints, progress (Project's Resume as P6's suspend and resume), baseline, resources and assignments with cost, text fields as activity codes (path codes rebuilt as P6 code trees), every field P6 20.12 writes, whole-number ids and unique resource IDs (Project fills Initials with the name's first letter, so repeats get -2, -3), and Project's scheduling options so P6's first run gives Project's dates; on 143 Project files none breaks P6's import rules, every activity, link and code reads back, the recomputed schedule is equal on 2,509 of 2,509 open tasks, and MPXJ reads the same values from the XML and the XER on 2,518 of 2,520 tasks; six P6 files sent through Project XML and back return every activity ID, link and code (eval/p6xer-check-2026-11-21.md; not imported into P6 itself). Nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Screening metrics on the user's own file, not scheduling, contractual or legal advice. Missed tasks and BEI use P6's planned dates as the baseline because a single XER rarely carries the baseline project. Expected finish dates (P6 "use expected end dates") set the remaining duration as in P6 and are listed as a finding, since they absorb predecessor delay; checked on one public file. Multiple float paths follow P6's free-float style but are not compared with P6's own result (no public file stores one); resource levelling is a serial pass like P6's (not P6's code), so its levelled dates can differ from P6's; the risk ranges are the user's assumption, not data in the file, and resource limits and probabilistic branches are not modelled. Not affiliated with Oracle, Primavera, Microsoft or the DCMA.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/xer-schedule-check/)

## For agents

- Engine: `xer.mjs` `parseXer(decodeXer(bytes))`; `mspdi.mjs` `parseMspdi(text)` reads Microsoft Project XML into the same `{ tables }` (task_code is the Unique ID; summary tasks become PROJWBS; status date is the data date; baseline 0 is target dates), `parseSchedule(text)` picks XER or MSPDI from the text; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer)` (dates in wall-clock minutes, float in hours) and `drivingPath(result, projId)`; `dcma.mjs` `assess(xer, { projId })` returns `{ project, checks[14], extra, recompute, activities, drivingPath }`, `findingsCsv(report)` and `scheduleCsv(report)` (every open activity's recomputed dates, total and free float beside the stored values).
- `msproject.mjs` `mspdiText(xer, { projId, codeNames })` returns `{ xml, project: { id, name, dataDate }, counts: { activities, wbs, links, calendars, resources, assignments, manual, mandatory, deadlines, external, crossProject, spanLinks, codeTypes, codeAssignments, udfFields, udfValues }, warnings, taskUid, codeFields, udfFields }` (Microsoft Project XML; activity ID in Text1, activity codes in Text2..Text30 aliased to the code type name, UIDs in outline order); `activityCodeFields(tables, taskRow, codeNames, { room })`; `udfFields(tables, taskRow, { textFrom, takenAliases })` (activity UDFs as Number/Cost/Date/Text fields); `ptHours(h)`, `isoDate(min)`. `parseMspdi` returns task text fields as ACTVTYPE/ACTVCODE/TASKACTV and task Number/Cost/Date fields as UDFTYPE/UDFVALUE. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --to-project out.xml [--project CODE] [--code-names] [--json]`.
- `p6xer.mjs` `p6XerText(mspdiText, { projectId, activityIds: 'auto'|'row' })` returns `{ xer, text, counts: { activities, relationships, wbs, calendars, resources, assignments, codeTypes }, warnings, project: { id, name } }` (a P6 XER for import); `p6Problems(tables)` lists what P6's import would refuse; `FIELDS` holds P6 20.12's field lists. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xml --to-p6 out.xer [--project-id CODE] [--row-ids] [--json]`.
- `floatpaths.mjs` `longestPath(result, projId)` (Set of task_id), `finishActivity(result, projId)`, `floatPaths(result, targetId, { count })` returns `{ target, paths: [{ n, float, activities: [{ code, name, start, finish, tf, rf, link: { to, type, lag, float } }] }], unreached }` (hours), `floatPathsCsv(fp)`; `assess()` adds `longestPath: { count, p6Flagged, agree, onlyP6, onlyHere }`. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --float-paths [CODE] [--paths N] [--csv paths.csv] [--json]`.
- `calslack.mjs` `calendarSlack(xer, { projId })` returns `{ open, activities: [{ code, name, calendar, tfP6, tf, gain, lateFinishP6, lateFinish }], links: [{ pred, succ, type, lag, lagCalendar, predCalendar, succCalendar, succLateFinish, succMayFinish, gap }], leavesCritical, maxGain }` (hours); `calendarSlackText`, `calendarSlackCsv`; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer, { calendarSlack: true })` is the engine option behind it (off by default: P6's dates). CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --calendar-slack [--csv slack.csv] [--json]`.
- `milestones.mjs` `milestoneCalendars(xer, { projId })` returns `{ open, milestones: [{ code, name, type, calendar, sits, logicGives, hours, successors: [{ code, calendar, start, couldStart, hours }] }], activities: [{ code, name, calendar, start, couldStart, hours, tf, tf24 }], gainFloat, maxGain, leavesCritical, finishes: [{ project, finish, finish24, moved }] }` (hours on each activity's calendar): milestones whose own calendar's non-work time holds back a successor on another calendar, and what a 24-hour milestone calendar gives back; `milestoneCalendarsText`, `milestoneCalendarsCsv`; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer, { milestones24h: true })` is the engine option behind it (off by default: P6's dates). CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --milestone-calendars [--csv held.csv] [--json]`.
- `evm.mjs` `earnedValue(xer, { projId, result, pvCuts })` returns `{ measure: "cost"|"hours"|null, currency, dataDate, totals: { bac, pv, ev, ac, etc, eac, sv, cv, spi, cpi, eacCpi, eacCpiSpi, vac, tcpi, pctPlanned, pctEarned, pctSpent }, earnedSchedule: { es, at, spit, svt, pd, ieacDays, ieacDate }, curve: [{ date, pv, ac, forecast, dataDate }], wbs, activities: [{ code, name, wbs, status, pct, bac, pv, ev, ac, etc, eac, sv, cv }], findings: [{ id, name, note, count, items }], notes }`; `percentComplete(taskRow, evType?, evUserPct?)`; `earnedValueText`, `earnedValueCsv`, `sCurveCsv`, `sCurveSvg`. Finding ids: unloaded, actual-not-started, remaining-finished, progress-no-cost, earned-ahead, overrun, actuals-from-progress, eac-under-actual. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --earned-value [--csv activities.csv] [--curve s-curve.csv] [--json]`.
- `evmseries.mjs` `earnedValueSeries([{ xer, label }], { projectName })` returns `{ project, measure, currency, baseline, updates: [{ label, dataDate, bac, pv, pvBaseline, ev, ac, eac, spi, spiBaseline, cpi, spit }], windows: [{ n, from, to, dataDateFrom, dataDateTo, earned, promised, performance, baseline, spiBaseline, spent, cpi, budgetChange, behind, ahead, costlier, budgetChanged, earnedTakenBack, actualReversed, added, removed, levelOfEffort }], total, warnings, notes }`; `earnedValueSeriesText`, `earnedValueSeriesCsv`. `earnedValue(xer, { pvCuts: [minutes] })` also returns `pvAt`. `status.mjs` `statusAsPlanned(xer, projId, dataDate, { slips, overruns, costs })` posts cost and units with the work. CLI: `node cli.mjs --windows u1.xer u2.xer ... --earned-value [--csv ev-windows.csv] [--json]`.
- `constraints.mjs` `parseConstraintLog(text)`, `evaluateConstraints(log, ctx)` (called by `lookahead(xer, { constraints })`, which then returns `constraintLog: { items: [{ row, codes, what, type, owner, expected, status, links: [{ code, needBy, latest, slackDays, status, past, slackOnly, alreadyBehind, moves, latestLoose, latestRelaxed }], finishSlipDays }], summary, finish: { base, withLog, slipDays } }` and per activity `openConstraints`, `startWithLog`), `constraintLogCsv`, `pastLabel(link)`. CLI: `--lookahead 3 --constraints log.csv [--constraints-csv updated.csv]`.
- `tia.mjs` time impact analysis (AACE RP 52R-06): `parseFragnet(csvText)` reads `Activity ID,Name,Duration,Predecessors,Successors,Not before,Event,Calendar` (columns by name; links `A1030`, `A1030 SS`, `F1 FS+2`, lags and durations in working days; `+N` on an existing activity adds N days); `timeImpact(xer, fragnet, { projId, expectedFinish })` returns `{ project, finish: { base, impacted, delayDays }, milestones: [{ code, name, base, impacted, delayDays }], fragnet: [{ code, name, kind, days, start, finish, floatDays, driving }], consumed: [{ code, name, floatBefore, floatAfter, usedDays }], absorbed (activities whose expected finish date absorbed the delay), drivingPath, fragnetOnPath, byEvent: [{ event, finish, delayDays }], overlapDays, warnings, impactedXer }`; `timeImpactText`, `timeImpactCsv`, `timeImpactHtml(r, { event, by })`; `xerText(r.impactedXer)` is the impacted schedule for P6. CLI: `node cli.mjs update.xer --tia fragnet.csv [--csv impact.csv] [--html tia.html] [--xer impacted.xer] [--no-expected-finish] [--json]`.
- `gantt.mjs` `gantt(xer, { projId, result, baseline })` returns `{ project, rows: [{ kind: "wbs", key, parent, depth, code, name, start, finish, count, critical, longest } | { kind: "task", key, parent, depth, id, code, name, type, status, start, finish, remStart, actualTo, milestone, span: "LOE"|"WBS summary"|null, tf, critical, longest, pct, preds, baseStart, baseFinish, variance }], from, to, baseline: "file"|"planned", summary, warnings }` (dates in minutes, variance in working days); `spanDates(result, xer)` gives level of effort and WBS summary activities their P6 dates; `visibleRows(g, { level, collapsed, expanded, critical, longest, search })`; `ganttSvg(g, view)`, `ganttHtml(g, view, { by })`, `ganttCsv(g)`, `ganttText(g, view)`; `gantt(xer, { groupBy: ["Responsibility", "wbs"] })` groups by activity code types (name or id) and/or the WBS, outermost first (group rows carry `level`, the result `groupBy`); `actvcodes.mjs` `codeTypes(xer, projId)` lists the types a project can use. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --gantt [--baseline base.xer] [--html gantt.html] [--csv gantt.csv] [--level N] [--critical] [--links] [--group-by CODE,WBS] [--codes] [--json]`.
- `lookahead.mjs` `lookahead(xer, { weeks, from, projId, result })` returns `{ project, weeks, from, through, days: [{ day, date, weekday }], activities: [{ code, name, wbs, status, start, finish, remainingHours, tf, ff, critical, resources, constraints, bars, ready, waitsOn: [{ code, type, lag, state, inLookahead, driving, date }], drivenBy, note }], summary, warnings }`; `lookaheadText`, `lookaheadCsv`, `lookaheadHtml(la, { by })`. CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --lookahead [WEEKS] [--from YYYY-MM-DD] [--html sheet.html] [--by NAME] [--csv lookahead.csv] [--json]`.
- `compare.mjs` `compare(prevXer, curXer)` returns `{ previous, current, finish: { moved, halfStep, progressEffect, revisionEffect }, flags, progress, logic, durations, constraints, calendars, activities, float, criticalPath }`; `compareCsv(rep)`, `compareText(rep)`.
- `windows.mjs` `windows([{ xer, label }, ...])` returns `{ project, updates, windows: [{ n, from, to, dataDateFrom, dataDateTo, workingDays, finishFrom, finishTo, moved, halfStep, progressEffect, revisionEffect, pathAtStart, drivers: { progress, revisions } }], total: { moved, sumOfWindows, progress, revisions }, recurring, warnings }`; `windowsText(rep)`, `windowsCsv(rep)`. CLI: `node cli.mjs --windows u1.xer u2.xer u3.xer [--report review.html [--appendix]]` (the review is of the latest update, compared with the one before it, with the windows in it). `xer.mjs` `xerText(xer)` writes parsed tables back to XER text.
- `report.mjs` `reviewItems(assessment, comparison?, risk?, windows?)` returns the ranked corrections `[{ severity, source, action, measure, items }]`; `riskItems(risk)` the risk-based ones alone (thresholds in `RISK_LIMITS`); `windowItems(windows)` the windows-based ones (thresholds in `WINDOW_LIMITS`); `reviewHtml(assessment, comparison?, { recipient, reviewer, reference, notes, date, limit, risk, windows, appendix })` returns a self-contained, script-free HTML review to print or save as a PDF.
- `risk.mjs` `riskAnalysis(xer, { projId, iterations, range: { min, likely, max }, correlation, ranges, risks, seed })` returns `{ project, percentiles[{ p, date, days, overDeterministic }], pDeterministic, pMustFinish, histogram, activities[{ code, name, criticality, sensitivity, deterministicCritical }], risks[{ id, probability, targets, occurred, finishShift, shiftNoise, notNoise }], withoutRisks{ percentiles, pDeterministic, eventDelay }, warnings }`; `parseRisks(csvText)` reads `id,probability,min,likely,max,activity...` (probability as 0.3 or 30%, days); `parseRanges(csvText)` reads `code,min,likely,max` in working days; `riskAnalysisAsync` runs in slices for a page; `riskCsv(result)`.
- CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --risk [N] [--range 90,100,125] [--correlation 0.3] [--ranges ranges.csv] [--ranges-udf auto|"opt,likely,pess"] [--risks register.csv] [--seed S] [--csv drivers.csv] [--json] [--report review.html]` (with `--report` the review carries the risk section; also with `--previous`); `node cli.mjs schedule.xer [--report review.html [--to NAME] [--from NAME] [--ref TEXT] [--notes TEXT]] [--json] [--csv out.csv] [--schedule activities.csv] [--project CODE]`; `node cli.mjs current.xer --previous previous.xer [--json] [--csv changes.csv] [--project CODE]` (the previous file's project is matched by project ID; CSV cells that would run as spreadsheet formulas are written as text).

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/xer-schedule-check): MIT licensed. Measurements: `eval/cpm-vs-p6-2026-11-19.md`, `eval/p6xer-check-2026-11-21.md` (Project XML to P6 XER: 143 Project files and six P6 files round-tripped; MPXJ agrees on 2,518 of 2,520 tasks), `eval/msproject-udfs-2026-11-21.md` (activity UDFs through Project XML: 42,971 of 42,971 values back, MPXJ agrees on every cell), `eval/msproject-codes-2026-11-21.md` (activity codes through Project XML: 276,042 of 276,042 values back, MPXJ agrees on every one), `eval/activity-codes-2026-11-21.md` (Gantt grouped by activity code: 92 charts on four public files, every activity under its file value), `eval/gantt-check-2026-11-20.md` (Gantt chart: level of effort and WBS summary dates equal P6's on 305 of 305; WBS rollups, coverage and planted baseline variances), `eval/tia-check-2026-11-20.md` (time impact analysis: planted fragnets on six public files against answers reached another way), `eval/earned-value-2026-11-20.md` (earned value on the public files: percent complete equals P6's computed actuals on 2,020 of 2,020 activities; curves close on budget and EAC), `eval/evm-series-check-2026-11-20.md` (earned value by window on update series built from the public files with planted slips and overruns), `eval/lookahead-check-2026-11-19.md` (look-ahead windows against P6's stored dates on seven files), `eval/calendar-slack-2026-11-20.md` (float P6's late dates miss across calendars: 188 activities on the hotel file, each checked by rescheduling), `eval/milestone-calendars-2026-11-20.md` (milestones on their own calendars holding back successors on other calendars: 8 on the hotel file, 1 on Expressway; every float gain checked by rescheduling), `eval/constraints-check-2026-11-20.md` (constraints log what-if against P6 start-on-or-after constraints on six files), `eval/constraints-slack-2026-11-20.md` ("past late start" read against calendar slack and missed deadlines: 65 of 65 rows classified as the reschedule shows), `eval/longest-path-2026-11-19.md` (longest path against P6's stored flag; the float-path backward pass against total float), `eval/free-float-2026-11-19.md` (free float equals P6's on 19,820 of 19,822 activities), `eval/compare-check-2026-11-19.md`, `eval/windows-check-2026-11-19.md` (windows analysis on update series built from the six files with planted delays), `eval/review-report-2026-11-19.md` (the written review on the six public files), `eval/risk-check-2026-11-19.md` (the risk run on the same six files), `eval/risk-register-check-2026-11-19.md` (risk register events: planted events against the CPM engine), `eval/cpm-vs-project-2026-11-19.md` (Microsoft Project XML: 102 files, 2,406 of 2,491 tasks equal Project's dates and float), `eval/resource-calendars-2026-11-21.md` (resource calendars and Resume dates: 2,442 of 2,491), `eval/review-risk-check-2026-11-19.md` (the risk section and its corrections in the written review on the six files), `eval/udf-ranges-check-2026-11-19.md` (ranges read from P6 UDFs: no real UDF misread, planted ranges = pasted CSV on 24 of 24 runs), `eval/review-windows-check-2026-11-19.md` (windows section, its corrections and the appendix in the written review, through files on disk and the CLI), `eval/converter-files-2026-11-19.md` (245 public XER files written by converters, other tools and by hand: 241 read with no crash or stray NaN, 4 non-P6 files refused with a reason).
